target.title: fix(extensions): bound success-path JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three success-path response reads still used unbounded `response.json()` / `resp.json()`. A compromised or buggy endpoint returning a multi-GB body on HTTP 200 buffers the entire body before `JSON.parse` even runs, OOMing the agent. The error path in the same files already uses a bounded reader; the success path was the inconsistent outlier.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same partial-hardening pattern already shipped across `comfy`, `anthropic-oauth`, `sms`, `matrix`, `telegram`, and `discord/api.ts`. The three remaining sites are the obvious next batch (the other two sites in the source triage — minimax/oauth and mattermost/client — were already bounded on `main`).

## User Impact

No behavior change for well-formed responses (small, valid JSON still parses). A huge or non-JSON success body is now truncated at a cap and handled gracefully instead of buffering in full and OOMing. thread-ownership (409 conflict body, 8 KB cap — still cancels on a truncated/malformed body), discord webhook ({id, channel_id}, 8 KB cap — fallback to {}), and huggingface model discovery (/v1/models, 256 KB cap — fallback to bundled catalog) all apply the same `readResponseTextLimited + JSON.parse` pattern already used by their error paths.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Three success-path reads used unbounded `.json()`, buffering the full body with no size cap — a huge body could OOM before parsing.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `162c068257` on branch `fix/unbounded-success-json-reads`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-per-site.mjs` — imports the real `readResponseTextLimited` (the helper now used by all three patched sites) and exercises each site's changed code path over real `Response` objects.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-per-site.mjs

  --- [thread-ownership] 409 conflict body (8 KB cap) ---
    well-formed 409: owner="other-agent" -> cancel (owner parsed)
    truncated 409 : owner=undefined -> cancel (409 semantics preserved)

  --- [discord/send.webhook.ts] webhook response (8 KB cap) ---
    well-formed response: id="msg-1" channel_id="C123"
    non-JSON response  : payload={} (fallback to {})

  --- [huggingface/models.ts] /v1/models body (256 KB cap) ---
    well-formed /v1/models: data.length=1 -> process
    oversize /v1/models : read capped, parse failed -> fell back to bundled catalog: true

  Verdict: all three patched sites enforce a read cap with a graceful fallback;
    thread-ownership 409 still cancels on a truncated body.
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** At every site, a small well-formed body still parses cleanly. A huge or non-JSON body is capped by `readResponseTextLimited`; the resulting JSON.parse failure is handled by each site's fallback logic. thread-ownership (8 KB cap): a truncated 409 body still cancels (the 409 status itself means another agent owns the thread; owner is logged as "unknown"). discord webhook (8 KB cap): a non-JSON webhook response falls back to `{}`, preserving the prior `.catch(() => ({}))` tolerance. huggingface (256 KB cap): an oversize /v1/models body falls back to the bundled catalog, matching the `!response.ok` branch.
- **What was not tested:** A live huge response from each real upstream (the real `readResponseTextLimited` helper over real `Response` objects is the faithful unit). Regression coverage: thread-ownership/index.test.ts (22 tests, incl. truncated-409-cancels), huggingface/models.test.ts (8 tests), discord send.webhook tests (3 shards, all passed).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts     (22 passed)
$ pnpm test extensions/huggingface/models.test.ts          (8 passed)
$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.proxy.test.ts  (all passed)
```

## Risk checklist

- Cap sizes: thread-ownership 8 KB (409 body is ~30 bytes); discord webhook 8 KB (reuses existing error-body cap; id+channel_id is tiny); huggingface 256 KB (real /v1/models ~150 KB, 256 KB gives generous headroom while still bounding a compromised endpoint).
- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended, bounded) — a huge/non-JSON success body is now capped + handled instead of buffering in full; well-formed responses unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Yes (improvement) — bounds response-body reads on three success paths, mitigating OOM from a compromised/buggy upstream.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) — touches three extensions; each uses the shared `readResponseTextLimited` already used by its own error path.
- Highest-risk area: a legitimately large-but-valid success body exceeding the cap would fall back — but all three success payloads are tiny in practice (well under their caps), and the prior behavior was an OOM crash, so the fallback is strictly safer.
- Mitigation: existing thread-ownership (22) + huggingface (8) + discord webhook tests pass + node runtime verification proving the cap is applied per site.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
